predecessors.name: March of Tuscany
predecessors.text: Lucca province, the Republic whose territories 'included the Garfagnana to the north'

successors.name: Principality of Lucca and Piombino
successors.text: Lucca province, the Republic whose territories 'included the Garfagnana to the north'

ledger.x: 1160: Lucca buys its feudal rights from Welf VI.
1316: Castruccio Castracani becomes lord of Lucca.
1316: the lordship of Castruccio Castracani begins (infobox 1316-1328); in 1325 Lucca's forces beat the Florentine army at Altopascio.
1328: Castruccio's lordship ends (infobox 1316-1328); the republican form returns until the loss of the city in 1335.
1335: Mastino II della Scala acquires Lucca.
1400: Paolo Guinigi overthrows the republican government.

23 June 1805: the republic is disestablished and Napoleon takes over its government ('In 1805, the governance of Lucca was taken over by Napoleon'); the French authority is the Directory in 1799, the Consulate and then the Empire.
23 June 1805: the Republic of Lucca ends (infobox 'Disestablished: 23 June 1805'); Lucca is merged with Piombino into the Principality of Lucca and Piombino.

wars.name: Battle of Altopascio
wars.outcome: Lucca's forces under Castruccio defeated the Florentine army and chased it 'up to the walls of Florence'.

wars.name: Florentine siege of Lucca
wars.outcome: Florence besieged Lucca in 1429 and again in 1430 'to take revenge on the republic'; the page gives no result and no 1433 treaty.
